question: Can the Commission share whether any EU laws adopted since 2019 have reduced the cost of living of EU citizens?
Can the Commission provide an estimate on the reduction in EUR per citizen?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.6.2024) In the EU, ensuring price stability is the primary responsibility of central banks. At the same time, inflation and purchasing power issues are a key consideration for the Commission’s policy agenda. The Directive on adequate minimum wages1 should help mitigate the impact of high inflation on workers by improving the adequacy of minimum wages.

The temporary Support to mitigate Unemployment Risks in an Emergency was a crucial element of the comprehensive strategy to protect citizens and mitigate the severely negative socio-economic consequences of the coronavirus pandemic.

Measures put forward under NextGenerationEU, REPowerEU and the Social Climate Fund include a strong social dimension to address the direct impact of the pandemic and of the energy price increases, but also to build social resilience in the longer term. The Commission has also made a number of country-specific recommendation with a bearing on poverty, social inclusion and social protection.

The 2023 Recommendation on adequate minimum income ensuring active inclusion2 promotes adequate income support and effective access to enabling essential services for persons lacking sufficient resources.

In the 2024 Euro area recommendations3, the Commission also advocated that Member States, in accordance with national practices and respecting the role of social partners, support wage developments that mitigate purchasing power losses, especially for low-income earners, taking due account of competitiveness dynamics and avoiding lasting divergences within the euro area.
While these measures and recommendations are all relevant to improving living and working conditions for Europeans, it is not possible to estimate their impact per household.
1 Directive 2022/2041 of 19 October 2022 on adequate minimum wages in the European Union, OJ L 275,

25.10.2022, p. 33–47. 2 Council recommendation of 30 January 2023 on adequate minimum income ensuring active inclusion, OJ C 41, 3.1.2023, p. 1-12. 3 https://commission.europa.eu/document/download/a5889ec5-4f8a-4294-a981dea13c763f6e_en?filename=COM_2023_903_1_EN_ACT_part1_v7.pdf
